Record Class OrderStatusEvent

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
app.order.event.OrderStatusEvent
Record Components:
accountId - the account the order was placed against; the message key, not part of the body
orderId - the order
status - ACCEPTED, FILLED or REJECTED
symbol - the instrument's ticker
side - BUY or SELL
quantity - units ordered
price - the price the order was filled at, or would be; currently the indicative price
rejectionReason - why the order was rejected, or null otherwise
occurredAt - when the order reached this status
public record OrderStatusEvent(Integer accountId, Integer orderId, String status, String symbol, String side, BigDecimal quantity, BigDecimal price, String rejectionReason, OffsetDateTime occurredAt) extends Record
One order reaching a committed status: ACCEPTED when the trading rules passed and the order was recorded as a firm commitment (BR-06), then FILLED or REJECTED when execution resolved it. An order the rules reject goes straight to REJECTED. OrderService and OrderExecutionService raise it inside the transaction that made the change, and TradeEventPublisher sends it to Kafka once that transaction has committed, so a consumer never sees a status the database does not.

The record is the message body as well: serialised as JSON it carries every component except accountId, which travels as the message key so that one account's events share a partition and keep their order. It holds plain values, not entities, because it is handled after the transaction and outside any persistence context.
